content:
maria: Heads up — after the eu-west rollout yesterday we're seeing kubelets in the edge pool flapping during startup. Pods can't resolve control-plane service intermittently, causing GPU nodes to fail bootstrap. :frowning_face:
ryan: do you have example logs? dns errors or connection refused?
maria: lots of `dial tcp <ip>:443: i/o timeout` and `lookup api.redwood-internal.svc.cluster.local: no such host` in kubelet logs. Happening only when sidecar proxy is present on node pods.
sasha: likely egress policy on sidecar is denying outbound to cluster DNS / service IPs. Did the new per-namespace egress policies roll out?
jamal: yep — we rolled egress-locked namespace policy for edge-tenant-* last night. It does default-deny + only allowed to egress via egress-gateway.
ryan: if gateway can't reach kube-dns or node metadata we get bootstrap failures. can we confirm the gateway has SNAT to the node pool's nat ip?
maria: `kubectl -n infra get pods -l app=egress-gateway -o wide` shows pods on same subnet but logs show `upstream connect error or disconnect` to 10.96.0.10:53
infra-bot: deploy 1977632100 completed for infra/egress-policy at 2026-02-12T03:14:07Z
sasha: quick workaround — allow exceptions for kube-dns (10.96.0.10) and metadata IP 169.254.169.254 in the sidecar egress policy. Also need to allow nodeport range 30000-32767 for health checks.
jamal: patch applied: `kubectl patch egresspolicy edge-tenant-locked -p '{"spec": {"exceptions": ["10.96.0.10/32","169.254.169.254/32","0.0.0.0/0:30000-32767"]}}'` — testing now.
ryan: can we also check Envoy cluster config? `kubectl -n edge exec -it <sidecar-pod> -- curl -s localhost:15000/config_dump | jq '.configs[] | select(.name=="cluster_manager")'` might show blocked clusters.
maria: after patch, 3/4 nodes bootstrapped successfully. One still stuck with `dial tcp 10.96.0.10:53: i/o timeout` — looks like conntrack exhaustion on that node.
jamal: I'll cordon + drain and rotate NAT on that node. adding alert to runbook: when egress-locked rollout, check gateway SNAT and kube-dns exceptions. :memo:
ryan: followup: can we add a canary for egress-locked policy to dev namespaces before cluster-wide rollout? this would've caught it.
maria: agreed. thanks all. re-opening for postmortem thread in eng-infra once stable.
leo: :thumbsup:
